title: The Flute Melody of Manik Raitong (Ka Sur Manik Raitong)
cultural_context: Ballad narrating the life of Manik Raitong, the destitute youth who played divine, sorrowful melodies on his Sharati bamboo flute by night. When queen Lieng Makaw fell in love with him, he chose death on the funeral pyre rather than compromise clan law, playing his flute into the flames.
lyrics_khasi:
Miet man ka miet u tem la ka sharati,
Sur ba pait-dohnud sawa ha ki lum,
Ka mahadei ka shah thap ha ka ieit,
U Manik u leit sha ka ding ha ka kuna.

Ha khlieh ka pyngkat u thad la ka sur,
Ym don ba tip ïa ka jingsngewsih jong u,
Tang ka sharati ka pynpaw ïa ka jingim,
Kaba khuid kum ka umjer ha u tiew-kulab!
lyrics_english:
Night after night he played his mournful Sharati flute,
A heartbreaking melody echoing through the mountain pine ridges,
The Queen was entranced by the irresistible power of love,
Manik stepped with royal dignity into the blazing pyre.

Atop the ash heap he poured forth his musical soul,
None understood the depths of his hidden sorrow,
Only the bamboo flute gave voice to his mortal existence,
Pure as morning dew resting upon the wild rose petals!

stanzas.title: Ka Sur Sharati (The Melancholic Night Flute)
stanzas.khasi:
Miet man ka miet u tem la ka sharati,
Sur ba pait-dohnud sawa ha ki lum,
Ka mahadei ka shah thap ha ka ieit,
U Manik u leit sha ka ding ha ka kuna.
stanzas.english: Every night he played his flute; heartbreaking notes echoed through the hills. Entranced by love, Manik faced the flames with unbending honor.

vocabulary.sharati: Long end-blown bamboo flute played during mourning and solemn reflection
vocabulary.raitong: Destitute orphan, poor person with no earthly possessions
vocabulary.mahadei: Consort or queen of a traditional Khasi Syiem
vocabulary.kuna: Clan fine, penalty, or sacrificial atonement
